result:
Neither solution's final value holds up, but Solution A is closer to correct.

**Solution A** uses a valid space barrier. Let $S = A_1\cup A_2\cup A_3$ with $|A_i|\approx 2n/3$, and forbid edges lying entirely in $S$. Then $|S| = 2n+1$, and a perfect matching would have to cover all of $S$ with $n$ edges, each meeting $S$ in at most 2 vertices. That covers at most $2n$ vertices of $S$, a contradiction, so no perfect matching exists.

The error is in the spectral computation. The bipartite link of $v\in A_1$ has block quotient $\begin{pmatrix}0 & b\\ a & b\end{pmatrix}$ with $a = 2n/3$ and $b = n/3$, which gives $\lambda^2 - b\lambda - ab = 0$. Its largest root is $\rho = 2n/3$, not $\sqrt{(5+\sqrt{17})/18}\,n \approx 0.712n$. The entries of $MM^T$ in Solution A are miscomputed (the correct matrix is $\tfrac{n^2}{9}\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$, with largest eigenvalue $4n^2/9$). So this barrier gives $c \ge 2/3$, and Solution A's stated value is wrong. Still, its framework is the right kind of extremal construction.

**Solution B** claims $c = (\sqrt5-1)/2 \approx 0.618$. This is contradicted by the space barrier above: it has no perfect matching and minimum link spectral radius $2n/3 > 0.618n$. Any valid threshold must therefore be at least $2/3$, so $0.618$ cannot be the constant. Its parity construction is also asserted rather than verified.

Both answers appear to be incorrect. The true constant is plausibly $2/3$, which is consistent with the barrier I checked, but I have not verified that no stronger barrier exists. Solution A at least rests on a valid construction, so it is the more likely of the two to be right.

WINNER: A
